description: Curated grading-evaluation dataset for Helga's Socratic grader. Each case has an expected FSRS grade (1=Again, 2=Hard, 3=Good, 4=Easy). Grades are ordinal, so the eval reports both exact-match and within-1 accuracy.

cases.question: Why do plants need sunlight to make their own food?
cases.student_answer: Because sunlight provides the energy that chlorophyll captures to split water and convert carbon dioxide into glucose. Without light there's no energy input to drive the reaction, so the plant can't build sugars.

cases.question: A passenger lurches forward when a car brakes suddenly. Explain why, and connect it to a broader principle.
cases.student_answer: The passenger keeps moving at the car's original speed because objects resist changes in motion — that's inertia. It's really Newton's first law: without a net force on the body, it continues in uniform motion, and the seatbelt is what supplies the stopping force the brakes applied only to the car.

cases.question: What were the main causes of the French Revolution?
cases.student_answer: Taxes, the king, bread, and the Bastille.

cases.question: What distinguishes an acid from a base?
cases.student_answer: Acids have a low pH and bases have a high pH.

cases.question: What does the derivative of a function tell you about the function?
cases.student_answer: It gives the instantaneous rate of change — the slope of the tangent line at a point. So if the derivative is positive the function is increasing there, and if it's zero you may be at a maximum or minimum.

cases.question: What is recursion in programming?
cases.student_answer: It's when you use a for loop to repeat code a fixed number of times.

cases.question: Why does the price of a good tend to rise when demand increases but supply stays fixed?
cases.student_answer: Because more buyers compete for the same limited quantity, so sellers can charge more and the ones willing to pay the higher price get the good. The price keeps rising until the quantity demanded falls back to match the fixed supply.

cases.question: Why do objects of different mass fall at the same rate in a vacuum?
cases.student_answer: My favorite planet is Saturn because it has rings.

cases.question: How does passive voice differ from active voice?
cases.student_answer: Passive voice is when the sentence sounds weaker or more formal.

cases.question: Why does ice melting in a warm room increase the entropy of the system?
cases.student_answer: Because the rigid, ordered crystal lattice breaks apart into liquid water where molecules can move and arrange in far more ways. More accessible microstates means higher entropy, and heat flowing from the warm room into the ice drives that increase in disorder.

cases.question: Why is binary search faster than linear search on a sorted array?
cases.student_answer: Binary search is faster than linear search because it searches faster.

cases.question: Why is DNA replication described as semi-conservative?
cases.student_answer: Because each new DNA molecule has two strands.

cases.question: Why can the probability of A given B differ from the probability of A?
cases.student_answer: Because knowing B occurred can change the set of outcomes we consider — we restrict to the world where B happened. If A and B are related, that restriction shifts how likely A is; only when they're independent does conditioning on B leave A's probability unchanged.

cases.question: Why do sodium and chlorine form an ionic bond?
cases.student_answer: Sodium has one loosely held outer electron and chlorine needs one to complete its shell, so sodium gives its electron to chlorine. The resulting positive and negative ions attract each other electrostatically, and that attraction is the bond.

cases.question: What is a metaphor and how does it work?
cases.student_answer: A metaphor is a figure of speech. It compares things.

cases.question: What does O(n) mean for an algorithm?
cases.student_answer: It means the algorithm always runs in exactly n seconds.

cases.question: Why does a cell placed in pure water swell?
cases.student_answer: Because water moves across the membrane from where it's more concentrated (the pure water outside) to where it's less concentrated (the salty cytoplasm inside), trying to equalize concentration. Water flooding in raises the internal volume and the cell swells.
